hero.headline: More Charges Likely After Stuart Tow Yard Shooting, Chase, Crash
hero.teaser: Jade Rondon, a Miami resident, now faces multiple felony charges after opening fire at Garry's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road in Martin County on Friday, a shooting tha
hero.body:
Jade Rondon, a Miami resident, now faces multiple felony charges after opening fire at Garry's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road in Martin County on Friday, a shooting that triggered a lockout at Murray Middle School and sparked a chase that ended when another woman, Valerie Valdes, crashed on US-1. The Martin County Sheriff's Office says additional charges against Rondon are likely as detectives continue reviewing video and phone and vehicle search warrants.

 According to the Sheriff's Office, Rondon arrived at the tow yard around 1 p.m. with Valdes to retrieve a car that had been involved in criminal activity Thursday evening before being reported stolen. Detectives had recovered the car Friday morning. When the vehicle's owner arrived to pick it up, an argument broke out between Rondon's group and another party.

 Sheriff John Budensiek said the dispute centered on belongings left in the car. "They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car which by the way the only thing really in the car was a couple guns," Budensiek said. Rondon then retrieved a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing in the car with Valdes.

 The people who were shot at also left before deputies arrived. Garry Reed, owner of Garry's Towing and Recovery, said an employee in his office was left shaken. "Young lady who works in my office — she was terrorized," Reed said.

 "The young lady went to see what was going on and all of a sudden she heard gunfire," he said, adding, "Scary. I'm racing — my heart is racing."

 Because the tow yard sits near Murray Middle School, the Sheriff's Office immediately activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout. Road patrol deputies, aviation units, detectives and other personnel searched for Rondon's car and located it on Cove Road near US-1. When deputies tried to stop her, Rondon fled, and deputies used a PIT maneuver to bring her car to a stop.

 Valdes, driving separately, was reportedly driving recklessly and lost control, causing a significant crash near Osprey Street and US-1. No one was seriously hurt in the crash.

 Rondon faces two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving with a suspended license and felony criminal mischief. Valdes faces charges of operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. Budensiek said investigators are still working to understand the full chain of events.

 "We're honestly not sure what we have," he said. "We're sure that shots are fired. We're sure that she fled from our deputies.

 Something happened with that vehicle the night before. There was a reason why everyone had interest in that car." The Sheriff's Office says more charges are possible as search warrants are processed and video evidence is reviewed. Reed said he was relieved no one was killed. "Thank God that everybody was okay," he said.

cards.headline: More Charges Likely After Stuart Tow Yard Shooting, Chase, Crash
cards.teaser: Jade Rondon, a Miami resident, now faces multiple felony charges after opening fire at Garry's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road in Martin County on Friday, a shooting tha
cards.body:
Jade Rondon, a Miami resident, now faces multiple felony charges after opening fire at Garry's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road in Martin County on Friday, a shooting that triggered a lockout at Murray Middle School and sparked a chase that ended when another woman, Valerie Valdes, crashed on US-1. The Martin County Sheriff's Office says additional charges against Rondon are likely as detectives continue reviewing video and phone and vehicle search warrants.

 According to the Sheriff's Office, Rondon arrived at the tow yard around 1 p.m. with Valdes to retrieve a car that had been involved in criminal activity Thursday evening before being reported stolen. Detectives had recovered the car Friday morning. When the vehicle's owner arrived to pick it up, an argument broke out between Rondon's group and another party.

 Sheriff John Budensiek said the dispute centered on belongings left in the car. "They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car which by the way the only thing really in the car was a couple guns," Budensiek said. Rondon then retrieved a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing in the car with Valdes.

 The people who were shot at also left before deputies arrived. Garry Reed, owner of Garry's Towing and Recovery, said an employee in his office was left shaken. "Young lady who works in my office — she was terrorized," Reed said.

 "The young lady went to see what was going on and all of a sudden she heard gunfire," he said, adding, "Scary. I'm racing — my heart is racing."

 Because the tow yard sits near Murray Middle School, the Sheriff's Office immediately activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout. Road patrol deputies, aviation units, detectives and other personnel searched for Rondon's car and located it on Cove Road near US-1. When deputies tried to stop her, Rondon fled, and deputies used a PIT maneuver to bring her car to a stop.

 Valdes, driving separately, was reportedly driving recklessly and lost control, causing a significant crash near Osprey Street and US-1. No one was seriously hurt in the crash.

 Rondon faces two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving with a suspended license and felony criminal mischief. Valdes faces charges of operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. Budensiek said investigators are still working to understand the full chain of events.

 "We're honestly not sure what we have," he said. "We're sure that shots are fired. We're sure that she fled from our deputies.

 Something happened with that vehicle the night before. There was a reason why everyone had interest in that car." The Sheriff's Office says more charges are possible as search warrants are processed and video evidence is reviewed. Reed said he was relieved no one was killed. "Thank God that everybody was okay," he said.
